plan.rationale: Torch already ran (66441/66441 kernels associated on the parent discovery), and the task is single-GPU with no communication, so nccl_tuning, collective_calibration and per-collective telemetry dimensions are not applicable. The observed uncertainty is candidate-side: evaluation.json's interpretation states the route labels are candidate-reported telemetry, not native proof. Specifically, (1) trial-recovered-19ccfe875f declares 728 fused-rms-norm / fused-rms-norm-gated route invocations across many call sites while the binding summary simultaneously reports effective 'direct' binding with reason 'no functional replacements' and functional_sites null, a direct contradiction over whether any replacement actually took effect; (2) trial-fc57bca7b9 declares 2 invocations of call 2441f10600ba127de5cb753c as 'parent-fallback:setup-failure:flash-dispatch-refused' plus 62 parent-delegate calls, with no independent exception evidence; (3) the candidate produced no valid clean measurement (quality_and_coverage_valid false, empty metrics, no_valid_parameter_candidate). candidate_diagnostics runs on this exact candidate and can verify declared routes against observed behavior, capture the actual setup-failure/flash-dispatch exception evidence, and inventory why the legacy binding found no functional replacements. nsys runs separately on the same candidate to corroborate kernel entries (fused RMSNorm kernels vs parent rms-norm kernels, and the fallback path's kernels) and attribute kernels to the prefill-to-first-token interval, addressing the route-attribution question the torch parent trace cannot answer for this revision. execution_timeline is not selected because the torch trace already provides submit association and its CPU-submission clock bounds do not resolve route validity; python_runtime is not selected because the binding is effectively direct (no dispatch/binding cost question) and it perturbs execution; device_telemetry is not selected because device-wide utilization/PCIe readings cannot resolve route or attribution questions for this GPU-resident workload. Revision is set to the single listed candidate revision.
